description: Since v0.4. Usage accepted after pause capture is pending in the next segment and survives JSON restoration without replaying call events. Only usage and tool metadata are portable. report_count, successful_call_sequence and pending_compactions restore outside usage totals; overflow tools stay in the overflow list; rule_outcome replaces deferred when/properties evaluation. Internal sdk_trace_id and pending span_id survive JSON restore without replaying spans.

explicit_credits.description: A pending call's report-supplied credits survive JSON restoration through credits_explicit. Configure a credits hook that returns hook_credits for every call, restore the snapshot, record span (a tracing report of the same response ID that stands for call_count calls), then end. The span merges into the pending call, which keeps its explicit credits instead of the hook's.

aggregate_report_order.description: SDK-6942: a Python-written pending snapshot has an aggregate, an older span, and an intervening report. Optional report_sequence is omitted to exercise legacy readers. Restore it, merge second with a 10-token wrapper at 200..210 ms, report third gpt-4o-mini with 20 tokens at 300..310 ms, end. Report order, never aggregate call counts, ranks primary model and outcome.

cross_sdk.description: A pending_calls record uses the same matched and usage_known keys in the three SDKs. Node and Python write started_at / ended_at in epoch milliseconds; Go writes RFC3339Nano UTC text until released Go readers accept numbers. All three readers accept both encodings. The timestamp-epoch-ms and timestamp-rfc3339 entries differ only in these timestamps and must restore the same timing, event ordering and counts. Each snapshot holds the same two calls recorded during paused-response delivery with emitLlmCalls on, as its written_by SDK writes them: a span with known usage and a wrapper call with unknown usage, both unmatched and timed. The two entries marked before SDK-6111 use the keys Python (started_ns, ended_ns) and Go (twin_matched, usage_unknown, RFC 3339 times) wrote until then, which every reader still accepts. For each snapshot: restore it with emitLlmCalls on, record reports in order (source wrapper or span, started_ms / ended_ms in epoch milliseconds), then end. Each report merges into its pending twin in the restored run, so expected.response is a subset of the final ai_response_received and expected.call_events lists a subset of each ai_llm_response_received, in order. Each SDK also writes the scenario itself and compares its pending_calls with its own entry. Top-level primary and outcome_hint use Node objects in current snapshots, legacy positional lists in the old entries; a persistent primary override and a cancelled outcome survive twin merges in either arrival order.

roundtrip.description: Actual snapshots from the current branch writers and released Node/Python 0.14.0 and Go v0.10.0 writers. Normal, overflow and suppressed-tool-rule variants exercise optional fields. Restore, end twice, keep the ID, and count each held call/tool once. No pending field written by a released writer is JSON null.
